steps.title: Enforce Authorized Access (AC.L1-3.1.1)

control_coverage.gap_rationale: Not met. Manual work required — Enforce Authorized Access

what_to_do: → M365: Use Compliance Manager CMMC assessment template to document access control policy
→ Portal: compliance.microsoft.com > Compliance Manager > Assessments
→ M365: Configure Entra ID as identity provider with Lifecycle Workflows for automated provisioning/deprovisioning
→ Portal: entra.microsoft.com > Identity > Users > Lifecycle Workflows
→ M365: Create Entra ID Access Reviews for all privileged and standard access on quarterly schedule
→ Portal: entra.microsoft.com > Identity Governance > Access Reviews > New access review

[CMMC Guidance] - Prefer tenant-wide controls.
- Document deviations and compensating controls with rationale.
- Use repeatable exports/logs instead of one-off screenshots.
[Assessment Design] Design for auditability: Implement the control so evidence can be produced on demand (policy + configuration export + operational logs) without manual reconstruction.
[Common Pitfall] Policies exist but are not enforced by configuration.
[Common Pitfall] Evidence is ad-hoc (screenshots) instead of repeatable exports/logs.
[Common Pitfall] Scope boundaries exclude systems that still touch CUI workflows.
[Deliverable] Compliance Policy Document
Content: Purpose, scope, and applicability to CUI environment
Content: Roles and responsibilities (policy owner, enforcers, affected personnel)
Content: Policy statements: specific, measurable, enforceable requirements
Content: Enforcement: consequences for non-compliance at each severity level
Content: Review cycle: at least annual review, change approval process, version history
Assessor: Policy exists, is current (within 12 months), and approved by appropriate authority
Assessor: Policy statements are specific and measurable (not vague aspirational language)
Assessor: Personnel have acknowledged receipt and have ongoing access to the policy
Assessor: Policy reviewed and updated at least annually with version history
Create with: Compliance Manager for policy scaffolding from CMMC assessment templates. SharePoint for document management with approval workflows, version control, and acknowledgment tracking.
Ref: NIST SP 800-171; NIST SP 800-53
[Deliverable] Access Review & Certification Process
Content: Review scope: all accounts with access to CUI systems and data
Content: Review frequency: quarterly for privileged accounts, semi-annual for standard
Content: Review process: manager certifies each direct report access as retain, modify, or revoke
Content: Documentation: reviewer name, review date, decision per account, follow-up actions
Content: Exception handling: orphaned accounts, service accounts, shared accounts
Assessor: Access reviews performed on schedule for the entire review period
Assessor: Manager sign-off documented for each reviewed account
Assessor: Revocation decisions implemented within defined SLA (e.g., 5 business days)
Assessor: Reviews cover both standard and privileged accounts including service accounts
Create with: Entra ID Access Reviews for automated manager certification campaigns. Entra ID Governance for automatic access expiration. Power BI for access review compliance dashboards.
Ref: NIST SP 800-171 3.1.1; NIST SP 800-53 AC-2

[Evidence] Collect "Joiner-mover-leaver (JML) procedure and samples" — acceptable forms: Procedure document, HR/IT tickets samples (redacted), Access removal evidence [assessor methods: examine, interview]
→ Collection guidance: Verify timeliness and completeness; sample terminations to confirm access removal across systems.
→ Retention: Retain procedure and sample records per audit period.
[Evidence] Collect "System Security Plan (SSP) completeness evidence" — acceptable forms: SSP document, SSP update log, Approval record [assessor methods: examine, interview]
→ Collection guidance: SSP must align with inventories/diagrams and reflect control implementation and inheritance.
→ Retention: Retain SSP versions and change log per policy.

[Evidence] Collect "Assessment boundary statement" — acceptable forms: Boundary statement document (PDF/Word), Scope memo / charter, SSP boundary section excerpt [assessor methods: examine, interview]
→ Collection guidance: Confirm boundary aligns with contract/flowdowns and matches diagrams/inventories; verify exclusions are justified and controlled.
→ Retention: Retain current version and prior version for change history; store approvals/sign-off records.
[Evidence] Collect "Network boundary diagram" — acceptable forms: Network diagram (Visio/PDF), Cloud network topology export screenshot [assessor methods: examine]
→ Collection guidance: Diagram should match actual configs (firewall/VNet/subnet rules) and reference where CUI traverses/terminates.
→ Retention: Retain diagram and source file; retain change log / approval ticket.

[Evidence] Collect "Endpoint security baseline configuration" — acceptable forms: Baseline policy export, Configuration profile export, Screenshot of settings in management console [assessor methods: examine, test]
→ Collection guidance: Demonstrate baseline definition and application scope; test a sample device for applied settings.
→ Retention: Retain baseline version history and change approvals.
[Evidence] Collect "Approved baseline standards (system hardening)" — acceptable forms: Baseline standard document, Hardening guide excerpt, Approved benchmark mapping [assessor methods: examine]
→ Collection guidance: Should be specific to OS/platform and map to how baselines are applied in tooling.
→ Retention: Retain version history and approval records.
[Evidence] Collect "Access review evidence" — acceptable forms: Access review report, Manager sign-off records, Remediation actions and closure proof [assessor methods: examine]
→ Collection guidance: Must show scope, cadence, reviewers, findings, and remediation actions; sample a review cycle end-to-end.
→ Retention: Retain reviews and remediation proof for defined retention period.

[Evidence] Collect "Security monitoring and alerting configuration" — acceptable forms: Alert rules export, On-call routing config, Sample alert and response ticket [assessor methods: examine, interview, test]
→ Collection guidance: Demonstrate that alerts trigger and are handled; ensure escalation paths are documented.
→ Retention: Retain alert configuration exports and sample response tickets.

[Evidence] Collect "Central log collection / SIEM ingestion proof" — acceptable forms: SIEM connector status screenshots, Log ingestion metrics export, Sample correlated event [assessor methods: examine, test]
→ Collection guidance: Include coverage (which sources) and health; test by generating an event and confirming ingestion.
→ Retention: Retain monthly ingestion/health reports; retain connector configuration change records.
[Evidence] Collect "In-scope asset inventory" — acceptable forms: CMDB export, MDM/Intune device inventory export, Cloud resource inventory export [assessor methods: examine, test]
→ Collection guidance: Inventory must be current and reconcilable to management tooling; sample a subset for existence and ownership.
→ Retention: Retain monthly snapshots for trending; retain inventory generation procedure.
[Evidence] Collect "Device management enrollment report" — acceptable forms: MDM enrollment export, Device compliance report, Management scope screenshots [assessor methods: examine, test]
→ Collection guidance: Include totals and a sampled subset; reconcile to in-scope inventory.
→ Retention: Retain monthly snapshots; retain enrollment procedure and exceptions.
